_comment: Phase D — 5 starter Structure recipes per STRUCTURE_DAMAGE_SPEC.md §7. Each recipe has a materialOf array (materialKey + qty) that the recipe engine consumes from a faction stockpile via game.bbttcc.api.factions.stockpile.adjust. footprintGrid drives token size. Special overrides: collapseProfile customization (e.g. Sept Bridge collapses at Damaged not Breached). | settlementTypes (2026-07-15, TOWNBUILDER_SPEC §6a): which hex types show this recipe in the Townbuilder menu; MISSING field = shows on every type.

recipes.name: Sept Wall (1 segment)
recipes.description: Baseline mass fortification — quarried highland stone over an anchored foundation, blessed thread woven into the courses, a single yesodium course at the core. Holds when the sept does.

recipes.name: Bunker Gate
recipes.description: Canonical fortress entry — scribed-steel gate leaves, hex-glyph plates pre-engraved along the seams, foundation cores at the threshold.

recipes.name: Watchtower
recipes.description: Tall, sparse — ash-wood frame on mountain stone footings, hex-iron cleats anchoring the platform, a focusing lens at the top.
recipes.specialNote: +1 detection rolls in the containing Hex

recipes.name: Glyph-Ward Pylon
recipes.description: A single dense column of hex-glyph plates around a sept tuning fork, with a tree-of-life shard at the apex. Radiates a faint warding field.
recipes.specialNote: +1 ward resist to all adjacent Structures (stackable)

recipes.name: Sept Bridge
recipes.description: Stone deck over ash-wood lattice, cold-iron lacing, single foundation anchor at the midspan. Falls hard.
recipes.specialNote: Collapse fires at Damaged state — the ravine is the whole point

recipes._section: SIEGE LAYERS — heavy fortress-grade walls purpose-built as breachable siege layers (high Plates + Threshold). The Strategic Siege engine stacks these as a besieged hex's structureActorIds; also buildable by hand from Rig Builder → Infrastructure → Fortifications.
recipes.name: Curtain Wall (siege layer)
recipes.description: The outer ring — a thick course of quarried highland stone over an anchored foundation, cold-iron lacing, blessed thread woven through. No sephirotic core, so it can be ground all the way down to rubble. The first thing a siege has to chew through.
recipes.specialNote: Outer siege layer (~142 Plates, no sephirotic → can be fully Razed). Pair as transitionRule 'razed' or 'threshold'.

recipes.name: Barbican Gate (siege layer)
recipes.description: The fortified gatehouse — scribed-steel leaves on hex-iron cleats, glyph-warded against breaching charges, set into a stone surround. The chokepoint where a storm gets bloody.
recipes.specialNote: Middle siege layer (~114 Plates, ward-resist vs breaching). Good as transitionRule 'threshold' (≤0.25).

recipes.name: Inner Keep (siege layer)
recipes.description: The last redoubt — a mass stone shell under dense glyph-warding and blessed courses, the garrison's final stand. Densely armoured but not load-bearing, so a determined storm can grind it all the way down.
recipes.specialNote: Innermost siege layer (~96 Plates, ward-resist, no sephirotic → fully Razable). Final layer — breach it to win the storm.

recipes._section: FLIMSY INFRASTRUCTURE — breakable scenery, not fortress walls. Mostly cloth/wood/salvage (low Plates, low Threshold so almost anything chips them), no sephirotic (so they can be fully Razed), light collapse profiles (a rig drives THROUGH these). facilityMode:false — these are scatter, not Holdings-scale facilities.
recipes.name: Wasteland Shack
recipes.description: A one-room hovel of scavenged board and salvaged sheet, draped in old cloth. Keeps the wind off. Keeps almost nothing else off.

recipes.name: Lean-To Shelter
recipes.description: A few poles, a hide, and optimism. Half a roof leaned against whatever was standing. The lightest thing anyone calls a home.

recipes.name: Shanty Hut
recipes.description: Corrugated salvage nailed to a timber frame, a bog-iron stovepipe poking through. Sturdier than a shack, still nothing you'd bet your life on.

recipes.name: Dilapidated Cottage
recipes.description: Pre-Fall mudbrick and rotten beams, half-reclaimed by the weather. Bigger and heavier than a shack, but the mortar is long dead — it comes down in slabs.

recipes.name: Market Stall
recipes.description: A trestle, a cloth awning, a board counter. Folds, splinters, and scatters the wares the instant anything heavier than a customer leans on it.

recipes.name: Wooden Fence & Gate
recipes.description: A run of plank fencing with a bronze-pinned gate. Marks a boundary, stops a wanderer, means nothing at all to a rig at speed.

recipes.name: Watchpost Shack
recipes.description: A raised plank box on stilts with a salvage-tin roof. Somewhere for a lookout to sit out of the rain — until something knocks the legs out.
recipes.specialNote: A perch, not a fortification — tips and drops its occupant when breached

recipes.name: Roadside Shrine
recipes.description: A little clay alcove with a blessed-thread offering, raised where someone died or something was promised. Small, soft, and oddly hard to bring yourself to flatten.

recipes.name: Fuel Shed
recipes.description: A salvage lean-to over a cache of jerry cans and seep-oil drums. Flimsy walls; very much not a flimsy thing to set on fire.
recipes.specialNote: Volatile — GM may rule that a fire-flavored breach detonates the stored fuel (area damage)

recipes.name: Salvage Depot
recipes.description: An open-sided rack-and-tarp pile of pre-Fall components waiting to be picked over. Lots of mass, none of it structural.

recipes.name: Water Tank
recipes.description: A riveted soft-alloy cistern on a low cradle. The metal skin dents and splits; what's inside does the rest.
recipes.specialNote: A breach floods the cell — GM may rule difficult terrain / a knockback wave below it

recipes.name: Generator Hut
recipes.description: A bog-iron housing around a coughing pre-Fall generator. Powers a few lamps, throws a few sparks, falls over like everything else out here.

recipes.name: Sandbag Wall
recipes.description: A stacked course of earth-filled sacks. Soaks up bullets and shrugs off small arms — then bursts and slumps when something heavy hits it.
recipes.specialNote: Good cover against fire (earth resists kinetic); concussive / ramming bursts it

recipes.name: Junk Barricade
recipes.description: A heap of welded scrap, fence wire, and dead engine blocks dragged across the road. Blocks a lane until someone with enough momentum disagrees.

recipes.name: Scrap Cover
recipes.description: A single hunched plate of bolted salvage — a one-person bit of cover to crouch behind. Lasts exactly as long as nobody focuses on it.

recipes.name: Palisade Fence
recipes.description: A line of sharpened ash stakes lashed upright. Stops a crowd, channels a charge — and burns or splinters readily.

recipes.name: S'narchy Burger Outpost
recipes.description: A reclaimed fast-food franchise turned frontier waystation. The neon mascot — a furious burger mid-obscene-gesture — still flickers sarcasm at passers-by; the drive-thru speaker has been rewired into a perimeter intercom. Sells certainty now instead of burgers. The booths make surprisingly good map tables.

recipes.name: Jackalope Trade-Post
recipes.description: A mercantile hub of stacked awnings, swinging scales, and at least three doors that are actually exits for when a deal goes sideways. The Jackalopes will weigh your goods, your worth, and your odds, in that order, and charge you for all three.

recipes.name: Leygate Anchor-Pylon
recipes.description: A tuned spire that grabs a passing leyline and holds it still long enough to walk through. Hums in a key that makes dogs sit and casters nervous. One yesodium core, one focusing lens, and a great deal of hope pressed into anchorstone.

recipes.name: Yesodium Containment Bunker
recipes.description: Where Khezek Tor keeps the ore that bites back. Rad-iron liner, cold-iron ribs, a hex-warded door that takes two to open and a lifetime to regret. Holds the glow in. Mostly. The dosimeter on the wall is decorative; the one in your bones is not.

recipes.name: Wendigo Ward-Fence
recipes.description: Salt below, vow-shafts above, hex-rope strung between and a smear of threshold-wax on every post. It will not stop a determined raider. It will give the things that are a bit OFF a reason to stay outside and sulk, which on the frontier is most of what a fence is for.

recipes.name: Pilgrim's Rest Chapel
recipes.description: A small Sephirotic waychapel — stone walls, blessed thread in the rafters, a single thread of sacred gold-leaf catching whatever light there is. The faithful sleep here safely. So does anyone else who can sit through the optional theology.

recipes.name: Battle-Bassinet Muster Yard
recipes.description: Where the Valhaulans rock their war-cradles into formation and sing the muster-lullaby loud enough to curdle morale three hexes out. Bog-iron stakes, herd-leather lashings, and a drum the size of an argument.

recipes.name: Repurposed Roadside Sign
recipes.description: An old highway sign stripped, rewired, and pointed at the horizon as a relay mast and lookout perch. Mal likes these — says it's nice to have somewhere to put the words. Reads the weather, the road, and your odds, and is wrong about exactly one of those at a time.

recipes._section: TOWNBUILDER PHASE 1.5 — type-flavored settlement buildings (TOWNBUILDER_SPEC §6b). Signature structures per hex type so each settlement menu feels like itself. facilityMode:true on the T2/T3 anchors, false on T1 scatter.
recipes.name: Grain Silo
recipes.description: A clay-daubed timber drum on stilts with a salt-lined throat. Holds the harvest, the seed-stock, and the town's entire argument for surviving winter. The mice have opinions; the cat is negotiable.
recipes.specialNote: A stocked silo feeds the hex — GM may waive travel rations provisioned here

recipes.name: Terraced Field Frames
recipes.description: Stepped planting boxes pegged into the slope and strung level with hex-rope, so the rain walks down politely instead of taking the topsoil with it. The frames are simple. The argument they settle with gravity is not.

recipes.name: Herd Byre
recipes.description: A warm-walled winter barn — timber over bog-iron footings, herd-leather weatherskirts, a salt-lick bolted by the door like a shrine to appetite. Whatever you graze out there sleeps in here, and the wall between you and it at night is exactly as thick as you paid for.

recipes.name: Adit Winch-House
recipes.description: A plank shed hunched over the mine mouth, all drum and rope and one lever worn smooth by nervous hands. Lowers the crew down in the morning. The whole town listens for how many turns it takes to bring them back up.

recipes.name: Ore Sluice
recipes.description: A long soft-alloy trough on a clay bed, running borrowed river through crushed stone until the worthless part leaves and the arguable part stays. Cold work, loud water, and every so often something in the riffles that makes the whole line go quiet.

recipes.name: Deep-Vein Rebreather Shed
recipes.description: Rad-iron lockers of pre-Fall breathing rigs, each one packed with living moss filters that eat what the deep seams exhale. Suit up, buddy-check, and mind the rule painted over the door: the moss goes home before you do.
recipes.specialNote: Working rebreathers — GM may ease Radiation exposure for crews delving from this hex

recipes.name: Ferry Slip
recipes.description: A stone-toed ramp and a rope-and-pole landing where the flat-bottom boats nose in. The schedule is a bell, the manifest is a shout, and the fare is whatever the ferryman decides you look like you can afford.

recipes.name: Dock Crane
recipes.description: A cold-iron jib on a timber tower, geared down so one stubborn person can swing a rig engine over the water and set it down like an apology. The counterweight is a rock with a name. Do not stand under the name.
recipes.specialNote: Heavy lift on the waterline — GM may speed rig loading/unloading through this hex

recipes.name: Harbormaster's Exchange
recipes.description: Stone below, scribed-steel shutters above, and a wall of courier-glass panes that flicker with the day's berths and debts. Every cargo on the water has a line here, written in oath-ink that itches when the manifest lies. The harbormaster has seen your paperwork. The harbormaster is not impressed.

recipes.name: Assembly Shed
recipes.description: A long open bay of benches, bins, and bronze-nailed jigs where salvage goes in confused and comes out purposeful. Nothing here is precise. Everything here is repeatable, which out here is better.

recipes.name: Press Line
recipes.description: A row of cold-iron presses driven off one salvaged heart-coil, thumping out plates, pins, and cleats in a rhythm the whole hex learns to sleep through. When the line stops, everyone wakes up. That is the alarm system.

recipes.name: Pattern Vault
recipes.description: A scribed-steel strongroom for the things a factory actually runs on: master templates, jig patterns, and pre-Fall reference pieces sealed in witness-resin so they remember being measured. Burn the town and it rebuilds. Lose the vault and it forgets how.

recipes.name: Field Archive
recipes.description: A weatherproofed reading shed — cloth-lined shelves, a ledger chained to the desk, and every entry made in oath-ink because field notes that lie kill people later. Smells of resin, dust, and the specific patience of whoever files the intake.

recipes.name: Instrument Loft
recipes.description: A raised observation floor stiff with tripods, lens-rigs, and courier-glass repeaters angled at the horizon, the leylines, and one another. Half the instruments measure the world. The other half measure the first half, which is how you know it's a real lab.

recipes.name: Resonance Cellar
recipes.description: A stone room sunk below frost line, quiet enough to hear the world's pitch. Tuning forks on anchor-quartz mounts, walls glazed in memory-resin that plays back yesterday's hum for comparison. Researchers whisper down here out of method. Everyone else does it out of instinct.
recipes.specialNote: Tuned to the local leyline — GM may grant advantage on leyline/resonance research made here

recipes.name: Open-Air Sanctum
recipes.description: A ring of standing stones threaded with blessing-cord, floored in wild herbs that bruise fragrant underfoot. No roof — the point is that nothing stands between the congregation and what they're addressing. Attendance is best in fair weather and most sincere in foul.

recipes.name: Bellframe
recipes.description: A timber tower hung with one great voice and a choir of brass thumb-bells, tuned against a sept fork so the whole peal lands in key. Rings the hours, the weddings, and the third pattern — the one nobody practices and everybody knows.
recipes.specialNote: Heard across the hex — GM may treat the peal as a settlement-wide alarm

recipes.name: Reliquary Walk
recipes.description: A covered stone colonnade of niches — finger-bones of the consented dead behind witness-glass, gold-leaf name-plates, threshold-wax seals renewed every festival. Pilgrims walk it slowly. Locals walk it daily, which the dead are said to prefer.

recipes.name: Common Hall
recipes.description: One big timber room the whole town fits inside, barely, on purpose. Meetings, weddings, trials, storm shelter — same benches, different seating charts. The door bar is oak and the agenda is whoever stands up first.

recipes.name: The Inn
recipes.description: Stone hearth, timber bones, leather-slung beds upstairs and a taproom below where the road empties its pockets and its rumors in the same motion. Every town wants one. The ones that have one can't remember being anything else.
recipes.specialNote: The road talks here — GM may surface travel rumors and hooks to guests overnighting

recipes.name: Bathhouse
recipes.description: Clay pipes, a soft-alloy boiler, salt-scrub basins, and stone benches in the steam where rank and grudge boil off with the road dust. Arguments are traditionally suspended past the second door. Traditionally.
